description: I am Angeline. I'm able to help with designs. I need members who can help with writing and storytelling.
summary:
Our team has created a short graphic novel titled The Adventure of Apollo 15. Through expressive artwork and heartfelt storytelling, this novel invites readers to step inside the boots of the brave astronauts who ventured far from home to drive across the silent, dusty plains of the Moon for the very first time. Rather than presenting spaceflight as a collection of cold numbers and distant dates, we bring the human spirit of the mission to life on every page.
Our project addresses the challenge by transforming complex lunar exploration into an intimate, emotional journey that anyone can experience. Many people feel disconnected from space science because it seems intimidating or out of reach. By focusing on the personal side of the mission, our visual story bridges that gap and awakens wonder, empathy, and excitement in readers of all backgrounds, letting them feel the genuine thrill of discovering an alien world alongside the crew.
This work is important because the future of space exploration depends on the dreams we inspire today. When young people feel a personal connection to the courage and awe of the Apollo 15 astronauts, the Moon stops being just a distant light in the night sky. Our short novel reminds every reader that exploration belongs to all of humanity and encourages the next generation to imagine their own place among the stars.
details:
Our team created an illustrated short graphic novel titled Moon Buggy: The Apollo 15 Adventure. Through expressive artwork and heartfelt storytelling, the novel invites readers to step inside the boots of Commander David Scott and James Irwin during their historic July 1971 mission to the Moon. It guides readers through key milestones of the mission—from deploying the 462-pound Lunar Roving Vehicle (weighing just 77 pounds in lunar gravity) and navigating crater rims with piano-wire tires, to traveling 17 miles and discovering the ancient "Genesis Rock." Rather than presenting spaceflight as a collection of cold numbers and distant dates, the story brings the human spirit of the mission to life on every page.

Many people feel disconnected from space science because technical data can seem intimidating or out of reach. Our project bridges that gap by transforming complex lunar exploration into an intimate, emotional visual journey that anyone can understand and enjoy. The intended impact of this work is to inspire the next generation of explorers. When young readers feel a personal connection to the courage and awe of the Apollo 15 crew, the Moon stops being just a distant light in the sky—reminding everyone that space exploration belongs to all of humanity.

To develop and design our comic, our team used SI tools such as:

• Story & Ideation: Gemini, Capcut and ChatGPT (for research refinement, narrative pacing, and scriptwriting)

• Visual Design & Layout: Canva (for illustrations)

We used a NASA data which is:

• NASA Image and Video Library (for images and clips for the project and video)

What makes our project creative is its focus on emotional storytelling and perspective. Instead of a standard textbook summary, we framed the Lunar Roving Vehicle as a character in humanity's first off-world road trip, ending with the poignant image of the buggy remaining on the Moon as a silent monument. During development, our team carefully considered historical accuracy (incorporating real mission dates, rover specs, and geological discoveries) alongside accessibility and visual appeal to ensure readers of all ages and backgrounds could easily engage with the science and history.
